submitter: bugfix_357_component_identity lane — RFC_046 PHASE 1, the write half of the provenance stamp. Owner ruled option 1 on 2026-08-22 ('Option 1 please, we can change the existing pages once option 1 has been built'). Code is committed and inert; this is the review, not a request to proceed.
rationale:
ROUND 3, and the shape has changed because the ARCHITECTURE QUESTION WAS SETTLED BETWEEN ROUNDS. Round 1 was gated as unsafe; round 2 was gated by editquality (HIGH, seconded by bug_historian) as ineffective — 'the mistyping mechanism and the Layer 2 carry-forward both continue to fire exactly as before; the diagnosed corruption is not stopped by this plan', and the 079/083 'detected but never blocked' recurrence. That objection was accepted, not argued. The architecture seat's own recommendation in that round — 'recommend an RFC scoping a durable component-instance identity rather than a fifth heuristic layer' — was filed as RFC_046 and the OWNER RULED IT: stamp identity at the point of production.

So this round is not another attempt to fix 357 with an inference. It is step 1 of a ruled two-step, and I want the council to judge it as that.

THE DEFECT, unchanged and cited: a page_components row's identity, bytes and content are written and carried as one bundle and no seam asserts they agree. Identity is re-derived by inference at every hop — from a data-component attribute, from the sentinel 'section' meaning unknown, from planned[Position-1], from fuzzy name matching, and from slot-name equality during a rebuild. 22 live rows (as of 2026-08-22) declare the shared `hero` while storing a whole interactive tool, newest born 2026-08-22 on a site homepage, because hero is planned first on all 22.

WHAT THIS CHANGE DOES: RenderTemplate — the estate's ONE render spelling, 15 non-test call sites as of 2026-08-22 — sets RenderContext.RenderedTemplateSHA to the SHA-256 of the template text it actually executed. That is the one fact only the seam knows, it is free (the seam has the text in hand), and it is REPORTED not acted on, because resolving it needs a database handle the seam does not have. RenderComponentAction emits it; extractSectionsFromMetadata carries it onto SectionData; resolveComponentVersionID turns it into a component_versions row id at the single INSERT INTO page_components, in the same statement as the bytes (IMP-052); carryStoredSection forwards an existing stamp so a carried row cannot silently downgrade to unknown.

WHY THE VERSION RATHER THAN THE COMPONENT: component_id records which component was ASKED; it does not record which template text RAN, and the two diverge the moment a template is edited. bugs_closed/277 closed with 15 rows permanently unrepairable because the templates that made their bytes exist nowhere — component_versions held zero rows for any of the nine components involved. This does not repair those. It stops the class accruing.

REUSE, NOT ADDITION, and this is the part I most want checked: page_components.component_version_id ALREADY EXISTS, purpose-built, and has never been wired. Measured 2026-08-22: 0 of 1,930 rows populated, no Go code writing it, no Go code reading it. No new column, no new table, no new concept. ⚠ site_plan_sections carries an identically-named column which IS live and accounts for nearly every grep hit — qualify by table or the dormant one looks busy.

plan.summary: Write-half only, and INERT BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing reads page_components.component_version_id (0 readers measured), so this cannot change what any page serves. IT DOES NOT FIX bugs_open/357 and the submission says so in those words — it builds the fact the fix is made of. Phase 2 (readers stop inferring: enrichSectionsWithPlannedNames may not name an unstamped section from planned[Position-1]) is where behaviour changes and is a separate round. Phase 3 (repair the 22) is owner-authorised in principle but blocked on the slot-name matching hazard phase 2 must resolve.

edits.rationale: The seam reports the digest of the template text it executed, computed BEFORE execution so it describes the input rather than anything the render may mutate. An OUT-FIELD rather than a return value, on the exact precedent of AbsentRequiredFields added by bugs_open/342: the signature was unified to ONE spelling across sixteen call sites by owner ruling 2026-08-21 and churning it again would undo that. The seam does NO I/O. An empty template returns early WITHOUT setting it — 'there was no template' is a kind of unknown, and stamping the digest of the empty string would hand a caller a provenance token pointing at a template that renders nothing. json:"-" because it must never be settable from content, and unlike InputSchema this field IS a string and so IS reachable by the reflection-derived step contract — the tag is doing real work here, and render_context_derivation_test.go is what tells you if that stops being true.

Turns what a section knows about its own provenance into a component_versions id, or into nothing. It returns ('',false) far more readily than it answers, and that IS the design: the only outcomes that produce a stamp are the two where provenance is a FACT — a carried stamp, or a digest still matching the component's current template. A template edited between render and save yields NO stamp and must never fall back to 'the component's newest version', because that would rebuild bugs_open/357's defect (a confident answer manufactured from something that merely correlates) inside its own fix. Get-or-create is keyed on the TEMPLATE TEXT, not the version number, so two saves of an unchanged template resolve to the SAME row and the table does not become a render log. ON CONFLICT (component_id, version_number) DO NOTHING covers the race with a concurrent save on another pod, which on this estate is the normal case, not the edge.

SectionData gains RenderedTemplateSHA (fresh render) and ComponentVersionID (carried). BOTH EMPTY MEANS UNKNOWN and unknown is persisted as NULL — nothing in this file may infer a version, for the same reason nothing should have been inferring a component. The stamp is written in the SAME statement as the bytes, beside md5($3), on the IMP-052 principle that the stamp and the thing it describes must not be two writes.
edits.sketch:
INSERT INTO page_components (page_id, position, rendered_html, rendered_html_digest, slot_name, component_id, content_data, content_brief, build_status, component_version_id)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, md5($3), $4, $5, $6::jsonb, $7::jsonb, 'deployed', $8)

edits.rationale: A carry does not change the bytes, so it must not change what produced them. Without this the save re-inserts a carried row with no stamp and a fact the estate already owned is lost on EVERY rerender — and rerenders are frequent here (one affected page had six in four days), so the stamp would erode faster than it accrued. This is the same file whose Layer 2 carry-forward is the conservation loop in bugs_open/357; the stamp joins the bundle it already forwards.

The half that matters is where it declines. Tests: a carried stamp is kept AND costs no query (asserted by sqlmock having no expectations at all); a malformed carried value is dropped rather than written on; no provenance means no stamp and no query; an unchanged template resolves to the existing row; first sight of a template records it. ⚠ THE DRIFT TEST USES A DECOY, and the obvious spelling of it does NOT work: written as 'expect no component_versions query' it passes against inferring code too, because sqlmock refuses the unexpected call, the resolver sees a query error, and it returns no-stamp for the wrong reason — a guard in series standing in for the one under test. So the decoy row is made AVAILABLE and attractive and the assertion is that the resolver does not take it, with TestComponentVersion_DecoyControl_AnInferringImplementationTakesIt as the paired control proving the decoy is genuinely on offer.

The bugs_open/229 pin ended at "'deployed')", which froze the statement's COLUMN LIST rather than the property it protects ('the digest is stamped in the same statement as the bytes', enforced by the separate `stamp` check). Adding a column reddened it without weakening anything it exists for, and a pin that reddens on a safe change trains the next author to widen it carelessly. Tail moved to "'deployed'". MUTATION-PROVEN rather than asserted: dropping md5($3) from INSIDE the matched span makes the check fail (anchor len 247→242, contains=false), and moving the statement makes it error on locate. The first mutation I ran was WRONG — I replaced the file's first md5($3), which is at line 994 and OUTSIDE this anchor, and the guard correctly still passed; the 'first occurrence wins' trap on source-scanning tests is exactly what that is.
edits.sketch: anchor: `(?s)INSERT INTO page_components \(page_id, position, rendered_html, rendered_html_digest,.*?'deployed'`

edits.rationale: Condition (2) of the platform-seams ruling: registered in the SAME commit that ships the seam. Records the landmine (the resolver refuses more than it answers, and why a fallback to 'newest version' would rebuild 357 inside its own fix), the decoy-test trap, the dormant-column reuse with the site_plan_sections name collision, and the verify-later with its control. CLC-025 was taken by another session mid-session, hence 026. The index ROW is added; the headline COUNT is deliberately not touched, because stored counts are retired and reintroducing one in the head of that file IS the finding.

plan.risks:
THE OBJECTION I EXPECT, AND I AM NOT GOING TO DODGE IT: this round, like round 2, does not stop the corruption. Every word of editquality's round-2 gating objection is still literally true of the code in front of you. The difference is not rhetorical and I want it judged rather than assumed: round 2 offered recording as a SUBSTITUTE for fixing, on my own initiative; this is step 1 of a two-step the owner ruled after the architecture seat referred the question, with step 2 named and its blocker identified. If the council's view is that a phase-1 write-half should not be reviewed separately from the phase-2 readers, say so and I will hold it and submit them together — but the code is already committed to the shared branch (this tree has no 'hold pending review'), so what that changes is the review unit, not what is on main.

SCOPE: this touches the fleet's busiest save path and the one render seam. Its defence is that it is INERT — 0 readers of the column, measured, so no page's bytes and no page's identity change. The one behaviour that does change is that component_versions gains rows it did not gain before (a get-or-create per newly-seen template text). Bounded: keyed on template TEXT, so an unchanged template resolves to the same row for ever. The disconfirming observation is stated in the register entry — a row count climbing on every render means the comparison is wrong and the table has become a log.

PERFORMANCE, since the guardian raised it last round about a hot path: the resolver issues ZERO queries for a section with no provenance and ZERO for a carried stamp, which between them are the overwhelming majority. It queries only for a freshly rendered section, and then at most three times, of which the INSERT arm fires once per new template text.

WHAT I HAVE NOT DONE AND AM NOT CLAIMING: no backfill of the 1,930 existing rows (they stay NULL, honestly unknown — and their staying NULL after the roll is the control that proves the stamp is coming from renders and not from a migration); no reader anywhere; no repair of the 22; and no change to any of the five inferences, which all still run exactly as they did.

STILL OPEN, unassumed: whether a full page rebuild THROUGH THE WRITER renders a hero template over a tool. Rerender demonstrably does not (six completed rerenders on vetcomparison.uk index 08-19→08-22 with the tool serving throughout, its rows re-created inside the 08-22 window). Nothing here establishes the writer path, and phase 2 must not assume it either way.
